items.title: 'Everyone is scared': Captain caught at the world's shipping chokepoint speaks out
items.description: For months seafarers have been stranded in the Strait of Hormuz, tanker captain Raman Kapoor is speaking out about the fears and uncertainty of his crew.

items.title: 'We are not leaving': What Israel's occupation could mean for Lebanon's future
items.description: Experts say Israel's continued presence in south Lebanon is creating a "bleak" future as it destroys villages in what it is calling a "buffer zone" and a "Forward Defense Line".

items.title: Live: US says it's 'on the brink' of deal with Iran, but uncertainty over peace talks remains
items.description: The White House says the United States is "on the brink" of a deal with Iran as the ceasefire deadline looms. Follow live.

items.title: Government to pay for showers for at-home aged care recipients
items.description: The decision to scrap the plan to charge older Australians $50/hour for showers was made after months of sustained criticism, including warnings that people were forgoing other care to afford the service.

items.title: States and territories left in the dark on NDIS savings
items.description: State treasurers say a meeting on NDIS reforms to be announced tomorrow was light on details, leaving states and territories waiting with everyone else to find out how a new round of savings measures will affect the disability scheme — and their budgets.

items.title: China suddenly grants new beef licences to Australia
items.description: China has granted beef export approval to several new Australian facilities, just months after introducing a range of trade measures to protect its domestic cattle industry.

items.title: Vanuatu warns Australia it will not be 'dictated to' after reports of China deal
items.description: As Australia presses on to finally sign a key agreement with Vanuatu, reports of a security agreement with China have drawn a fierce response from Port Vila.

items.title: Government pours $30m into counter-drone technology in wake of Iran war
items.description: The Australian government signs two contracts to develop counter-drone technology, including a laser that can track an object the size of a 10-cent coin travelling at more than 100 km/h.

items.title: Boyd says other AFL players are struggling 'under the surface' after Hollands episode
items.description: Tom Boyd, former AFL footballer turned mental health advocate, says the high-pressure environment of professional football means many players are struggling with mental health issues "under the surface".

items.title: Sacked civil servant describes pressure to approve Mandelson as UK ambassador to US
items.description: The former head of the Foreign Office said there was "a very, very strong expectation" that Peter Mandelson "needed to be in post and in America as quickly as possible".

items.title: 'Outrageous mess': About 2,000 AI road safety camera fines withdrawn in WA
items.description: About 2,000 fines valued at $1.1 million issued as a result of AI-assisted road safety cameras in WA have been withdrawn, six months after the devices were introduced.

items.title: Diesel and fertiliser are shooting up in price
items.description: There are two things crucial to modern farming - synthetic fertiliser and diesel.  So what happens when the cost of both increases massively, but the crops they're used to grow remains the same price? That's precisely the dilemma facing Australian farmers as they prepare to plant their winter crops for this year.  While some have chosen to opt out of the season entirely, others say they are pushing ahead and facing the uncertainty.

items.title: More uncounted votes discovered in SA a month after election
items.description: More uncounted votes have been discovered in two electorates a month on from the South Australian state election, and while the state's Electoral Commission says the ballots will not harm the "integrity" of the count, they have not said how many have been found.

items.title: Producer on Rebel Wilson film branded 'Indian Ghislaine Maxwell', court hears
items.description: Australian actor Rebel Wilson asked her crisis communications firm to publish a website that accused a producer on her own film of being an "Indian Ghislaine Maxwell", a Sydney court hears.

items.title: Six ways your smartwatch is lying to you, according to science
items.description: Wearable fitness technologies like smartwatches are worn by millions of people daily. But they're not as accurate as you might think.

items.title: Earthquake hits off coast of Timor
items.description: The epicentre was at a depth of 31 kilometres but there was no tsunami risk from the magnitude-6 quake, according to Indonesia's geophysics agency.

items.title: I quit TV for a month, but the trick was what I did with myself instead
items.description: It was partly an experiment in self-control and habit-breaking, but also a response to the unhappy realisation that watching shows had become my crutch to zone out.

items.title: Researchers develop surfboard fins with shark-deterrent technology
items.description: A multi-million-dollar project run out of the University of Wollongong is working on fitting shark-deterrent technology into surfboard fins following recent shark attacks.

items.title: Living in an apartment with your dog? Here are four things to consider
items.description: Providing opportunities for your dog to explore, giving them a safe and comfortable space to retreat to — as well as a good routine — are key to keeping your dog happy.

items.title: Woolworths's 'Prices Dropped' promotion broke guidelines, court hears
items.description: The consumer watchdog has taken Woolworths to court, claiming shoppers weren't receiving genuine discounts on hundreds of items.

items.title: Man jailed for mimicking shooting on bridge used in Bondi attack
items.description: A man who yelled antisemitic profanities while pretending to shoot at people from a pedestrian bridge used by the Bondi Beach terror attack gunmen has been sentenced.

items.title: Bitter with Australia for deporting him, he hatched a plan to get even
items.description: Eneasi Taumoefolau's 2024 arrest on drugs charges ignited fears the notoriously violent outlaw Comancheros gang had infiltrated "the Friendly Islands".

items.title: Last chance for answers as police admit error in search for Nannup Four
items.description: The family of a mother and daughter who went missing, along with two others, in WA almost 20 years ago are pinning their hopes on a last-ditch effort to uncover the truth of what became of them.

items.title: Legal action considered after Dezi Freeman property entry
items.description: Property owner considers legal action after people enter the Upper Murray property where Dezi Freeman was shot.

items.title: Rattenbury denies quitting over coalition talks, but they can't have helped
items.description: In announcing his retirement from ACT politics, Greens leader Shane Rattenbury says he is looking forward to finding out what his next career move could be.
